messages:
amy-support: Hey team, multiple customers in us-west are reporting 300-800ms spikes this morning. traces show some requests being routed through ap-southeast-1. attaching a minimal trace and sample headers.

amy-support: Trace snippet:
```
request_id=rc-9bf3c
route_hops=[us-west-2 -> ap-southeast-1 -> us-west-2]
x-route-hops: us-west-2,ap-southeast-1,us-west-2
latencies_ms=[12, 312, 8]
```

amy-support: Affected tenant: acme-corp, ~20% of their requests in the last 30m. No auth errors, just elevated p95.

deploy-bot: deploy 2024-06-25T07:10:23Z - nina-eng updated fallback/shard-priority (canary) - id=deploy-9876 :rocket:

jordan-sre: @amy-support can you paste a full response header (x-route and x-trace-id) for one of the slow requests? also example curl/traceroute if you have one.

amy-support: sample curl response headers for rc-9bf3c: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-request-id: rc-9bf3c
x-route-hops: us-west-2,ap-southeast-1,us-west-2
x-runtime-node: runtime-02
x-trace-id: trace-20240625-abc123
```

amy-support: traceroute to runtime-02 (from customer mgmt vpc):
```
1 10.1.0.1
2 52.24.10.4
3 203.19.5.33 ap-southeast-1 edge
4 54.213.17.7 us-west-2
```

kai-runtime: seeing the same in runtime logs for tenant=acme-corp: `route_hint=ap-southeast-1` stamped in router middleware when handling some sessions. looks like fallback/shard-priority might be assigning a temporary hint.

devon-net: Could be two causes: smart-router fallback policy (logic-level) or network-level egress change/peering. If traces sometimes hop regions, likely app-level routing selecting a remote shard for a subset of keys. Did we change any shard hashing or fallback order recently?

nina-eng: I pushed a canary PR earlier that adjusted fallback shards to prioritize capacity in ap regions when us-west saturates. PR: https://stash.redwood/infra/PR/4521 (canary). That change also added a sticky fallback token to reduce rebalancing thrash.

jordan-sre: ok that matches. sticky fallback token could cause some sticky routing to ap-southeast for keys that hit a fallback. can you repro locally with header override? run this to check header counts: 
```
for i in {1..20}; do curl -sI -H "x-tenant: acme-corp" -H "x-origin-ip: 3.101.22.5" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate | grep x-route-hops; done
```

amy-support: ran it from our support repro box (10 runs): results pasted: 
```
1: x-route-hops: us-west-2
2: x-route-hops: us-west-2,ap-southeast-1,us-west-2
3: x-route-hops: us-west-2
4: x-route-hops: us-west-2
5: x-route-hops: us-west-2,ap-southeast-1,us-west-2
6: x-route-hops: us-west-2
7: x-route-hops: us-west-2
8: x-route-hops: us-west-2,ap-southeast-1,us-west-2
9: x-route-hops: us-west-2
10: x-route-hops: us-west-2
```

kai-runtime: that pattern is consistent with sticky fallback: some requests get assigned a fallback shard in ap-southeast-1, then later get routed back when KV cache warms. i can add extra logging (fallback_token, chosen_shard, shard_reason) and roll a canary patch to runtime-02. need :+1: from eng to proceed.

nina-eng: please go ahead, roll the logging canary to 5% and let's observe p95. also add a temporary control-plane toggle to force region override for acme-corp if we need immediate mitigation.

devon-net: i'll also open a quick peering check with cloud-net-team to confirm there wasn't an underlying egress peering change this morning. logging will rule the config side in/out.

jordan-sre: executing quick mitigation: applying route override for tenant acme-corp -> region=us-west-2 via control plane (temporary). Command: `rdwctl route override --tenant acme-corp --region us-west-2 --ttl 1h`

amy-support: applied override, customers reported p95 back to normal ~10m after. re-running the curl loop shows no ap-southeast hops in 20 runs.

ops-bot: Alert cleared: route-variance-acme-corp - incidents/1462 - latency p95 back within baseline.

amy-support: thanks all — will follow up with a postmortem once canary logs are in. marking this thread resolved for now. :tada:
